title: Lesson 56 - Scalability and Efficiency: Performance Strategy in Practice
description: Recommend strategies for performance optimization strategies across all components (Omniscript load time, IP execution, Data Mapper queries) to ensure scalable and efficient solutions.

questions.question: A solution generates a large document inside an OmniScript and users report timeouts. What is the best fix?
options: Increase the OmniScript timeout to the maximum
Generate the document asynchronously and have the script confirm submission
Reduce the document size by removing required fields
Move the document generation to a FlexCard
questions.explanation: Generating the document asynchronously lets the OmniScript confirm submission and return control, which removes the synchronous wait and the timeout. Increasing the timeout only delays the failure. Removing required fields changes the business output. A FlexCard is a display component and does not generate documents.

questions.question: An architect is designing for a solution that will grow from hundreds to millions of records. Which practice best supports scalability?
options: Return full result sets so no data is ever missing
Keep queries selective and bounded, and cache read-mostly reference data
Run all work synchronously so results are always current
Store all external data in custom settings
questions.explanation: Selective and bounded queries plus cached reference data keep the solution within limits as data grows. Returning full result sets will hit row limits at scale. Running all work synchronously blocks users and does not scale. Custom settings are for configuration, not for storing large external datasets.

questions.question: A long-running Integration Procedure blocks the user's browser while it completes. What is the correct approach?
options: Keep it synchronous so the user sees the final result
Move the heavy work to asynchronous processing and let the script confirm submission
Duplicate the IP logic inside the OmniScript
Reduce the IP to a single Data Raptor
questions.explanation: Moving the heavy work to asynchronous processing lets the script confirm submission and return control, which is the scalable pattern. Keeping it synchronous preserves the block. Duplicating the logic adds maintenance without fixing the wait. A single Data Raptor cannot perform the external orchestration the IP does.
